test_title: PYST 8 - SSC CHSL 2025 - English Language (Held On: 14 Nov, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: english
question: Which of the following statements is grammatically correct?

options.text: The integration of AI into workplace raises questions regarding job loss, algorithmic bias, and the redefinition of human work.
The integration of AI into workplace raise questions regarding job loss, algorithmic bias, and the redefinition of human work.
The integration of AI into workplace raise questions regarding job losses, algorithmic bias, and redefinition of human work.
The integration of AI into workplace raises questions regarding job losses, algorithmic bias, and the redefinition of human work.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The subject of the sentence is **“integration”**, which is a **singular noun**; therefore, it requires a **singular verb** form.
 
• The correct verb form is **“raises”**. Hence, sentences using **“raise”** are grammatically incorrect due to **subject–verb disagreement**.
 
• Options **2** and **3** use the plural verb **“raise”**, which does not agree with the singular subject **“integration.”**
 
• Option **4** correctly maintains **subject–verb agreement** and also preserves **parallel structure** in the list: *job losses, algorithmic bias, and the redefinition of human work*.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• **Option 1** – Uses the correct verb **“raises”**, but the phrase **“job loss”** is less appropriate in a general discussion about widespread workplace impacts.
 
• **Option 2** – Incorrect because the verb **“raise”** does not agree with the singular subject **“integration.”**
 
• **Option 3** – Incorrect due to the use of the plural verb **“raise”** with the singular subject.
 
• **Option 4** – Grammatically correct as it maintains proper **subject–verb agreement** and consistent **parallel construction**.
